falsification.description: In mouse cortex or human iPSC-derived neuron/astrocyte/microglia co-culture, delete Csmd1 while measuring C4b/C3b deposition on synaptosomes and microglial engulfment of synaptic material; then rescue with soluble CSMD1 Sushi-domain protein. If CSMD1 loss does not increase synaptic complement deposition, and if C4A overexpression does not increase engulfment on a Csmd1-null background, the activator/inhibitor-ratio model fails.

readout.label: C3b/C4b deposition on synaptosomes and microglial synaptic engulfment

hypotheses.mechanism: The C4 structural locus is the strongest complement signal in schizophrenia genetics (rs116633139, p=6e-18, OR~1.16), and higher C4A copy number/expression increases C4 protein available to the classical cascade initiated by C1q. CSMD1, itself genome-wide significant (rs12541020, p=6e-9; Open Targets genetic score 0.81) and built from 28 Sushi/complement-control-protein domains, is a classical-pathway inhibitor expressed by astrocytes and at synapses. Risk therefore arises from the *ratio* of activator (C4A/C4B, C1QA) to inhibitor (CSMD1) at the synaptic surface: excess C4 deposition with insufficient CSMD1 restraint mis-tags synapses during adolescent pruning, thinning cortical connectivity. STRING confirms C1QA-C4A/C4B as a tight module enriched for classical complement activation, and Reactome scores 'Activation of C3 and C5' and 'Regulation of Complement cascade' as the set-level signal.
hypotheses.title: Elevated C4A/C4B dosage tips C1q-initiated classical complement tagging of synapses, and CSMD1 loss removes the brake

falsification.description: Quantify C1q/C3b deposition per synapse and microglial engulfment index in matched post-mortem prefrontal cortex from schizophrenia cases and controls, stratified by C4A copy number, using array tomography. The excess-pruning model (H1) predicts increased per-synapse complement deposition and increased engulfment in cases, particularly high-C4A cases; this hypothesis predicts reduced C1q deposition and reduced microglia-synapse contact. A finding of increased deposition falsifies H2.

readout.label: per-synapse C1q deposition and microglia-synapse contact

hypotheses.mechanism: The dominant narrative is complement excess, but the direct measurements point the other way: C1q protein is *lower* in first-episode psychosis and schizophrenia (PMID:38301948), complement gene expression changes divergently across brain regions (PMID:39616737), and schizophrenia-associated C4 has been reported to *decrease* microglia-synapse interactions via CR3 (PMID:41903141). C1qa-null mice show abnormal excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic currents, abnormal synaptic bouton morphology and absence seizures — a synaptic-refinement failure phenotype from loss, not gain. Combined with CX3CR1's microglia-restricted expression and its role in activity-dependent circuit sculpting, the hypothesis is that schizophrenia reflects degraded microglial surveillance/refinement — synapses that should be removed are retained and those that should be kept are lost — rather than a simple pruning excess.
hypotheses.title: The complement change in schizophrenia is a loss of tonic C1q/CX3CR1 surveillance, not a gain — mistimed rather than excessive pruning

falsification.description: Prepulse inhibition and cortical circuit recording in Nxph3 conditional knockouts restricted to deep-layer cortical excitatory neurons, alongside conditional Ccdc136 knockout. If deep-layer-restricted Nxph3 loss does not disrupt PPI/startle, the neuron-intrinsic arm collapses; if Ccdc136 knockout produces the same phenotype, the passenger-gene call is wrong.
falsification.system: conditional knockout mouse, deep-layer cortical excitatory neurons

hypotheses.mechanism: NXPH3 and CCDC136 sit outside the complement module entirely — STRING places them with zero edges to C1QA/C4A/C4B or to each other, and Reactome cannot map them at all. NXPH3 is a secreted neuropeptide-like ligand for alpha-neurexins expressed in brain excitatory neurons; its mouse knockout produces increased startle reflex, abnormal spatial learning and abnormal locomotion — schizophrenia-relevant endophenotypes (sensorimotor gating, cognition, psychomotor activity). CSMD1-null mice show the mirror-image decreased startle, so these two genes plausibly act on the same behavioural axis from opposite directions and via different molecular routes. CCDC136 is annotated only for acrosome/spermatogenesis function and has no GWAS association with schizophrenia; the most likely reason both appear in this list is positional co-occurrence at the chromosome 7q32 locus, not shared biology. This hypothesis is therefore explicitly about neuronal neurexin-complex signalling (NXPH3) and flags CCDC136 as probably a linkage passenger.
hypotheses.title: NXPH3 and CCDC136 mark a neuron-intrinsic, complement-independent arm: neurexin-ligand signalling in deep cortical neurons setting sensorimotor gating

falsification.description: Liver-specific versus brain-specific conditional deletion of C4 (or C4A humanised transgene expression restricted to hepatocytes) in mice, measuring CSF and synaptic C4 deposition and PPI. If hepatocyte-restricted C4 expression fails to produce detectable synaptic C4 deposition while astrocyte/neuron-restricted expression does, the peripheral-source model is dead and H1's brain-intrinsic version stands.

hypotheses.mechanism: HPA finds C4A and C4B predominantly hepatic and adrenal with minimal brain detection, while C1QA and CX3CR1 are microglial and C1QA is markedly choroid-plexus enriched. If brain C4 is largely imported rather than locally transcribed, the C4 risk allele acts on the CNS through systemic complement load and barrier/choroid-plexus handling, with microglia as the effector reading the imported signal. This predicts that peripheral C4 levels, not brain C4 transcription, track risk, and it reframes the therapeutic target: C4 itself is a poor CNS target, whereas CX3CR1 is a druggable GPCR with ligand-bound structures and high-quality small-molecule chemistry, and no immunomodulatory agent has yet been registered in the schizophrenia trials returned. The set-level enrichment for 'Differentiation of Circulating Monocytes' is consistent with a peripheral-myeloid contribution.
hypotheses.title: Peripheral, not brain-intrinsic: liver-derived C4 crossing a permeable barrier drives the association, making CX3CR1 the only tractable node
